title: Start April With a Clear Constraint
teaser: A useful constraint can keep a plan from expanding faster than your capacity.
full_text: Choose one limit for an April project today: time, budget, scope, or number of priorities. Write it where you will see it before adding new work.

title: Turn One Meeting Into a Decision
teaser: A meeting can feel productive while leaving the actual choice unresolved.
full_text: Before your next important meeting, write the single decision that should exist by the end. If no decision is needed, question whether the meeting is necessary.

title: Move Friction to the Right Place
teaser: Good habits benefit from low friction; risky habits often need more of it.
full_text: Make one helpful action easier to start today and one distracting action slightly harder. Change the environment instead of relying only on willpower.

title: Compare Purchases by Useful Life
teaser: A cheaper item is not always the lower-cost choice over time.
full_text: Pick one recurring purchase and estimate how long each realistic option would serve you. Compare total useful life, not just checkout price.

title: Check the Meaning Before the Tone
teaser: Tone is easy to misread when context is thin.
full_text: If a message bothers you today, first identify the literal request or information in it. Ask for clarification before building a conclusion around tone alone.

title: Remove One Unnecessary Handoff
teaser: Every handoff creates another place for delay or information loss.
full_text: Look at a repeated workflow and find one handoff that adds no distinct expertise or control. See whether ownership can stay with one person for that step.

title: Plan for the Week You Actually Have
teaser: An ideal week is a poor template when real commitments are already fixed.
full_text: Review the next seven days and mark immovable commitments first. Fit priorities into the remaining capacity instead of planning from an empty calendar.

title: Make Appreciation Specific Enough to Repeat
teaser: Specific recognition tells people what contribution mattered.
full_text: Thank someone today by naming the action you noticed and the effect it had. Avoid turning the message into a broad judgment about their personality.

title: Give a File a Clear Owner
teaser: Shared files become unreliable when nobody knows who keeps them current.
full_text: Choose one important shared document and record who owns updates, what 'current' means, and when it should be reviewed next.

title: Separate Probability From Impact
teaser: A dramatic outcome can distort judgment even when its probability is small.
full_text: For one risk today, rate likelihood and impact separately. Decide whether your response should reduce the chance, the damage, or both.

title: Test Learning With a New Example
teaser: Understanding is stronger when it transfers beyond the example you studied.
full_text: Take a concept you learned recently and apply it to a case you have not seen before. If the rule breaks, return to the underlying idea rather than memorizing another example.

title: Create a Restart Rule
teaser: Missing once does not need to become a new pattern.
full_text: For one routine, define exactly how you will restart after an interruption. Make the restart small enough to happen on the next realistic opportunity.

title: Match Decision Speed to Reversibility
teaser: Some choices deserve experiments; others deserve slower review.
full_text: Classify one pending decision as easy or hard to reverse. Use a faster test for the reversible one and more evidence for the costly-to-reverse one.

title: Ask for the Observable Example
teaser: Vague feedback is difficult to act on because the target keeps moving.
full_text: When you receive broad feedback today, ask for one specific moment, behavior, or output that illustrates it. Build the change from that example.

title: Cut One Midmonth Commitment
teaser: A plan can improve by subtraction before anything new is added.
full_text: Review the rest of April and remove, defer, or delegate one commitment that no longer earns its place. Protect the capacity you recover.

title: Clarify Who Can Say Yes
teaser: Teams stall when everyone can discuss but nobody can decide.
full_text: For one shared task, identify the person who can make the final call. Keep contributors and decision authority visible as separate roles.

title: Audit an Automatic Renewal
teaser: Automatic payments can continue long after their value becomes unclear.
full_text: Check one subscription today for renewal date, actual recent use, and cancellation terms. Decide before the renewal window becomes urgent.

title: Move Quality Control Earlier
teaser: Late inspection finds problems after they have become expensive.
full_text: Choose one repeated task and place a small verification step closer to where the error is first introduced. Compare the effort with fixing it at the end.

title: End a Message With the Needed Action
teaser: People should not have to infer what response you want.
full_text: Before sending an important message, add one clear final line stating whether you need an answer, approval, decision, file, or date.

title: Protect a Short Transition
teaser: Switching instantly between demanding tasks can carry unfinished attention forward.
full_text: Leave a brief transition between two focused activities today. Capture the next step from the first task before opening the second.

title: Verify the Source Behind a Number
teaser: A precise number can still be weak evidence if its origin is unclear.
full_text: Take one figure you plan to use today and record its source, date, and definition. If those are missing, treat the number as unverified.

title: State a Boundary Before It Is Tested
teaser: Boundaries are easier to respect when they are known in advance.
full_text: Communicate one upcoming limit on time, scope, or availability before pressure builds. Include what you can offer so the other person can plan around it.

title: Define What Would Change Your Mind
teaser: A test is stronger when the result can actually alter the decision.
full_text: For one belief or plan today, write the evidence that would make you revise it. If no possible result could change your view, it is not functioning as a test.

title: Standardize the Repeated Part
teaser: Templates should reduce repeated effort without erasing important differences.
full_text: Turn one recurring task into a short checklist or template today. Keep variable decisions outside the template so judgment still has room.

title: Pair a Metric With a Real Sample
teaser: Dashboards can hide the lived result behind an average.
full_text: Choose one quality metric and inspect a real example behind it. Check whether the example supports the story the number appears to tell.

title: Define the Finish Line for One Focus Block
teaser: A time block works better when it produces a visible output.
full_text: Before starting focused work today, specify the artifact or decision you expect at the end. Stop expanding scope once that output exists.

title: Name the Need Before the Request
teaser: Clear needs make requests easier to shape without turning them into demands.
full_text: Before asking someone for help today, identify what need you are trying to meet. Make a specific request while leaving room for a genuine yes or no.

title: Check the First External Dependency
teaser: A detailed schedule is fragile when its first dependency has not been confirmed.
full_text: For one plan, identify the earliest thing you need from another person, system, or supplier. Verify its availability before committing later dates.

title: Shrink the Problem to a Testable Unit
teaser: Broad problems invite broad solutions that are hard to evaluate.
full_text: Take one frustrating issue and narrow it to a specific condition, step, or time window. Change one thing and observe whether that smaller problem moves.

title: Close April With a Rule Worth Keeping
teaser: A useful month leaves behind more than a list of completed tasks.
full_text: Choose one rule, boundary, or system from April that improved your work or wellbeing. Decide where it will live in May so it does not depend on memory.
